bugs: Marking a task done without setting completed_at (e.g. $task->update(['status' => 'done'])) leaves completed_at null, so the task is never counted in tasks_completed_last_7_days. Nothing ties status to completed_at (app/Models/Task.php:17, probe confirmed)

The dashboard uses Cache::remember with no stampede protection. Concurrent misses after an invalidation all recompute the expensive query, and Cache::flexible was not used even though the task allows up to 5 minutes of stale data (app/Services/TeamDashboard.php:16)
antipatterns: app/Services/TeamDashboard.php:16 — Cache::remember plus a hand-rolled version key, where Cache::flexible([secs, 300]) would cover the 'stale OK if recompute is slow' requirement
app/Services/TeamDashboard.php:34 — the version key is itself stored with Cache::remember, so every dashboard read costs two cache round trips
app/Observers/TaskObserver.php:24 — a DB query on every task save just to find the team_id
app/Services/ExchangeRates.php:28-40 — manual block/try/finally release, where the block($secs, $callback) form is shorter
strengths: Routes go through routes/api.php with Sanctum, and guests get a 401 for both JSON and plain requests
Rotating a version key prevents the race where a reader computing old data re-caches it after a forget; the reason is stated in one tight docblock
Observers implement ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit, are registered with #[ObservedBy], and invalidate the previous team as well (getPrevious) when a project, task or user moves
UserObserver only invalidates when team_id changes or the user is created, so unrelated user saves don't flush the cache
Exchange rates: double-checked fresh cache under the lock, separate fresh and last-known keys, a failure cooldown, timeout(3), and lock timeout falls back to stale or 503
Strong Pest tests: an invalidation dataset covering 10 kinds of change, query-count assertions, failure datasets, and Sleep::fake lock-contention tests
FormRequest normalises case and exposes a typed currency() accessor; #[Scope] attributes and enum casts

bugs: A guest making a non-JSON request to /api/dashboard or /api/exchange-rates/{c} gets a 500 (RouteNotFoundException: Route [login] not defined), because the API routes live in web.php behind the session 'auth' middleware (routes/web.php:11, probe confirmed)

Cache::forget invalidation has a race: a reader that started computing before a write commits can re-cache the old data for up to 5 minutes, which breaks the 'reflected within seconds' requirement under concurrency (app/Support/TeamDashboard.php:40-44)

UserObserver::saved forgets the team dashboard on every user save, including unrelated changes such as name or remember_token, which causes needless recomputes on a hot endpoint (app/Observers/UserObserver.php:12, probe confirmed)
The dashboard uses Cache::remember with no stampede protection and does not use Cache::flexible despite the stale-tolerant requirement (app/Support/TeamDashboard.php:20)
antipatterns: routes/web.php:11 — API endpoints added to web.php under an 'api' prefix with the web middleware stack (sessions, CSRF), instead of install:api / routes/api.php
app/Observers/TaskObserver.php:13-16 — two separate queries on every task save, even when project_id did not change
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:4 — `use Closure;` in a non-namespaced file produces a PHP warning in the test run
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:175 — the 'three second timeout' test only asserts a config value and never checks the timeout actually applied
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:110 — the test says waiting requests reuse the lock holder's result, but it only checks a plain cache hit
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:16-20 — a mutable $this->upstream closure works around Http::fake, which is more indirect than Http::sequence
strengths: The Task saving hook keeps completed_at consistent with status (stamped when done, cleared when reopened)
Uses Cache::lock()->block($wait, $callback), which releases the lock automatically
DB::afterCommit defers invalidation until the transaction commits
Failed fetches are reported with report($e); timeout and lock wait are in config/services.php
Thin invokable controllers, a FormRequest with a typed accessor, and #[Scope] and #[ObservedBy] attributes
Tests cover timeouts via ConnectionException, malformed and empty bodies, cooldown recovery, and the 7-day window moving with travel()

v.rationale: Both suites pass (impl-1: 42 tests, impl-2: 41 tests). The two implementations are close in structure, so the ranking comes down to how robust the caching is and to the bugs the probes found. impl-1 ranks first. It puts the routes in api.php with Sanctum, so guests get a 401 for both JSON and plain requests. Its version-key rotation stops a reader from re-caching data computed before a write committed. Its observers fire after commit and skip unrelated user saves. Its tests are stronger, including lock-contention tests using Sleep::fake. Its main gap is that a task marked done without a completed_at is not counted as completed. impl-2 puts the API routes in web.php behind session auth, so a non-JSON request from a guest returns a 500 (probe confirmed). Its plain Cache::forget leaves the stale-recache race open. It also clears the dashboard cache on any user save (probe confirmed). Its tests are weaker: the 3-second timeout test only checks a config value, one test name overstates what it checks, and a `use Closure;` line causes a warning. On the plus side, impl-2 auto-stamps completed_at and uses the callback form of lock block(). Neither implementation uses Cache::flexible or protects the dashboard against a stampede.
